html:
Zimbabwe suffered one of the worst hyperinflations in history in the late 2000s, peaking in late 2008, when prices doubled roughly every day, and the country gave up its own currency in 2009.

The crisis followed the collapse of commercial farming after the land seizures, the costs of war in Congo, and the printing of money to pay the state. Shops emptied, millions left for South Africa, and a cholera epidemic spread.

The central bank issued a 100 trillion dollar note in 2009 before the Zimbabwe dollar was abandoned for the US dollar and the rand. New national currencies have since been tried and have lost value, keeping the memory alive in Zimbabwe under Mugabe and his successor.
sum: Zimbabwe suffered one of the worst hyperinflations in history in the late 2000s, peaking in late 2008, when prices doubled roughly every day, and the country gave up its own currency in 2009.
